heroSummary: The Bambu Lab A1 can print Polymaker PolyLite ASA at speeds up to 202 mm/s supported by an effective volumetric flow rate of 17 mm³/s. However, because the A1 is an open-frame bedslinger, successful printing requires mitigating ambient drafts or utilizing a draft shield/enclosure to prevent severe warping and layer separation.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with PVP glue stick or Magigoo as an adhesive and release interface
slicerTweaks: Set Bed Temperature to 98°C and Nozzle Temperature to 250°C to maximize inter-layer bonding near the A1 hardware limit.
Enable a 10 mm wide Outer Brim with 0 mm brim-object gap to mechanically restrain corners from lifting on un-enclosed beds.
Set Maximum Volumetric Speed to 17 mm³/s in the filament profile to prevent under-extrusion at high travel rates.
Configure Part Cooling Fan to 0% for the first 3 layers, keeping normal fan speed between 10% and 20% to prevent rapid thermal contraction.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Corner lifting and warping off the build plate
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: High thermal shrinkage coefficient of ASA exacerbated by open ambient air currents across the heated bed.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Increase bed temperature to 100°C, apply PVP glue stick on the Textured PEI plate, add a 10 mm brim, and enable a draft shield in OrcaSlicer.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Delamination and horizontal layer splitting mid-print
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive part cooling or low ambient temperature leading to poor thermal fusion between successive layers.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Reduce auxiliary and part cooling fan speeds to a maximum of 15% and lower printing speed by 20% to increase thermal dwell time.

troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Moisture absorption in the hygroscopic ASA filament converting to steam in the hotend.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament spool in a dedicated dryer at 70°C for 6 to 8 hours prior to printing, and set retraction to 0.8 mm at 30 mm/s.

faq.question: Can I print PolyLite ASA safely on an open-frame Bambu Lab A1?
faq.answer: Yes, but ASA emits styrene fumes and is prone to warping from ambient drafts; ensure printing is conducted in a well-ventilated area or tent enclosure away from room drafts.

faq.question: Do I need to upgrade to a hardened steel nozzle for Polymaker PolyLite ASA?
faq.answer: No, standard PolyLite ASA is non-abrasive, meaning the stock stainless steel nozzle on the A1 is completely compatible without premature wear.

faq.question: Why is the bed temperature limited to 98°C-100°C on the A1?
faq.answer: The Bambu Lab A1 has a hardware safety ceiling of 100°C for its bed; setting it to 98°C provides safe, stable thermal performance close to the glass transition temperature of ASA.

faq.question: Is an auxiliary cooling fan recommended for ASA prints on the A1?
faq.answer: No, auxiliary cooling fans should be turned completely off, as directional forced air causes immediate layer separation and edge warping in ASA.
